title: MiniCPM: Unveiling the Potential of Small Language Models with Scalable Training Strategies
data_curation: The stable pre-training stage uses ~1T tokens drawn mostly from open corpora: cleaned CommonCrawl-Chn, Dolma, C4, Pile, Wikipedia, Chinese books, Baidu Baike, Open Web Math, Arxiv, peS2o, Stack Exchange QA, and code from The Stack and StarCoder. Deduplication is performed within and across corpora using MinHash. The decay (annealing) stage shifts to a more diverse, higher-quality mix including UltraChat, SlimOrca, OssInstruct, EvolInstruct, ShareGPT4, plus proprietary Math/Code/Logic/Knowledge SFT data (LeetCode, K12 textbooks). Two BPE tokenizers (sentencepiece) are built: 122,753 vocab for the 2.4B model and 73,440 for the 1.2B model. For the 128K variant, data is split into long (books/wikis/papers, 44%) and short (56%) subsets, supplemented with synthetic long QA. Data curation emphasis is on the staged mix rather than a single pipeline, with the high-quality SFT data concentrated in the decay phase.
curriculum: Training is ordered as three stages with the Adam optimizer throughout: (1) stable training on ~1T coarse pre-training tokens at batch 3.93M and max LR 0.01 under the WSD scheduler; (2) a decay/annealing stage using exponential decay (f(s-T)=0.5^((s-S)/T), T=5000 steps ~20B tokens) over a mixture of pre-training and high-quality SFT data; (3) a separate SFT stage (~6B tokens) using SFT-style data with LR aligned to the end of annealing and again WSD decay. Ablations (A-1/A-2, B-1/B-2/B-3) show that injecting high-quality data during decay beats adding it only in SFT, even with more SFT tokens. For aligned variants: MiniCPM-DPO adds one epoch of DPO (LR 1e-5, Cosine LRS) after SFT; MiniCPM-128K reuses the last stable checkpoint with ABF then NTK RoPE and a 32K-to-128K curriculum; MiniCPM-MoE is built via Sparse Upcycling from the dense stable checkpoint then continued pre-train/decay/SFT for 130K steps.
method: The core contribution is the Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning rate scheduler: linear warmup to eta, a constant stable phase, then a decay phase f(s-T)*eta. This splits training into high-LR exploration and a distinct annealing phase, enabling continuous training without a predefined token budget and reuse of stable-stage checkpoints. Empirically the loss drops dramatically during decay, ~10% of total tokens suffices for annealing, and decaying from any stable checkpoint matches a Cosine schedule trained to that step. WSD makes scaling-law measurement linear-cost (O(mC)) rather than quadratic: training 6 model sizes (0.04B-2B) and decaying from 10N-60N data fits L(N,D)=C_N N^-alpha + C_D D^-beta + L0, giving alpha=0.29, beta=0.23 and a compute-optimal data/model ratio ~192x (vs Chinchilla's 20x). Supporting methods include Model Wind Tunnel Experiments (Tensor Program muP width/depth scaling, optimal batch-size law bs=1.21e9/L^6.24, stable optimal LR ~0.01), a two-stage pre-training strategy, DPO alignment, Sparse Upcycling MoE (2/8 experts, load-balancing loss x0.01), and Int4 GPTQ quantization for edge deployment.
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses the open UltraEval framework with vLLM inference across C-Eval, CMMLU (Chinese), MMLU (English), HumanEval, MBPP (code), GSM8K, MATH (math), HellaSwag, ARC-e, ARC-c (commonsense), and BBH (logic); QA tasks use both perplexity and direct generation, reporting the best. Chat quality is measured by MTBench (LLM-as-judge) and long context by InfinityBench. MiniCPM-2.4B ranks highest among SLMs on average, matches Mistral-7B in English and surpasses it in Chinese, and beats Llama2-13B except on MMLU/BBH/HellaSwag; MiniCPM-1.2B beats Llama2-7B except HellaSwag. MiniCPM-2.4B-DPO raises MTBench from 6.89 (post-SFT) to 7.25, surpassing Llama2-70B-Chat and zephyr-7B, at a small alignment-tax cost on benchmarks. MiniCPM-2.4B-128K matches Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 (ABF1000w) and beats ChatGLM3-6B-128K despite being 2.5x smaller. MiniCPM-MoE (13.6B total, 4B activated) is on par with Llama2-34B. Int4-quantized MiniCPM-2.4B runs at 18 tokens/s on an iPhone 15 Pro.
key_results: MiniCPM-2.4B (2.4B non-embedding params) surpasses Mistral-7B and Llama2-13B on average across C-Eval/CMMLU/MMLU/HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K/MATH/BBH. MiniCPM-2.4B-DPO reaches MTBench 7.25, beating Llama2-70B-Chat and zephyr-7B. The fitted scaling law yields a compute-optimal data/model ratio of ~192x versus Chinchilla's 20x, and MiniCPM-MoE (4B activated) matches Llama2-34B.
evolution_note: Building on Kaplan (2020) and Chinchilla (Hoffmann 2022) scaling laws and muP/Tensor Program hyperparameter transfer, MiniCPM reacts to Chinchilla's 20x data/model ratio by empirically recovering a much higher (~192x) compute-optimal ratio under modern overtrained configurations akin to Llama2. Its WSD scheduler and 'anneal on high-quality data' two-stage recipe presage the annealing-with-curated-data and continuous-training practices that became common in later 2024 small-model and efficient-scaling work.
